Is a QLED TV worth it? A QLED TV uses tiny particles that glow when lit, called Quantum Dots, to deliver higher brightness and more accurate, vivid colors. Because each dot emits a precise hue, QLED displays maintain rich color no matter how bright the screen. It’s worth getting a QLED TV if you want a more immersive experience for movies, sports, or gaming. QLED screens create a vivid viewing experience that really draws you into the action. What is the difference between QLED, OLED and Neo QLED TVs? The major difference between Samsung QLED, OLED and Neo QLED TVs is the lighting technology. QLED TVs use nanoscale-sized particles called Quantum Dots illuminated by a traditional backlight. This technology provides vibrant colors and good brightness levels. Neo QLED TVs also use Quantum Dot technology like QLED TVs, but their backlight design is made up of mini-LEDs for more precise lighting control. This enhancement allows for better contrast and darker blacks compared to traditional QLED TVs. Samsung TVs with QLED technology (including QLED, Neo QLED, and Neo QLED 8K TVs) have been certified by TUV Rheinland as having Real Quantum Dot Display, meaning that the elements that make up the display meet International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards. A Real Quantum Dot Display includes a Quantum Dot sheet, and blue LED. How long does a QLED TV last? QLED TVs use inorganic materials that put less stress on the screen, which helps prevent burn-in issues and contributes to longevity. Which is better, QLED TV or Crystal UHD TV? QLED and Crystal UHD both deliver bright, colorful HDR images, and 100% color volume but QLED TVs go further by using Quantum Dots—tiny particles that emit highly precise colors. This gives QLED TVs enhanced brightness and superior color accuracy, which tends to make them more expensive. A crystal UHD TV is still great for everyday viewing, but if your budget allows and you want a more immersive experience for movies, sports, or gaming, a QLED TV is the better upgrade. *100% color volume measured in Movie Mode and the DCI-P3 color space, certified by VDE.
